_README._comment: Deep-test-only zone definitions for the firewall/network test suite. These four zones used to ship in the INSTALL template (manager/network-manager/zones.json); ADR-014 D7 removed them from it — a test probe has no business on a production install — and they live here instead, next to the test that activates them. network/test.sh --deep merges these into the DEPLOYED zones.json (state Active), runs the inter-zone rule validation, then removes the keys again in cleanup_deep. Nothing else reads this file.
_README.tier_note: Typed and tiered like any other zone so the ADR-014 invariants (I1 monotonic access-to, I2 isolation floor, I4 archetype conformance) hold while they are temporarily live: testAllowA/B are trusted-client-shaped (tier 2) and testPinhole is a service-shaped target (tier 1) reached ONLY by pinhole — which is exactly the auto-pinhole path #173 exercises.
_README.dmz_note: testAllowA/B keep dmz in BOTH access-to and pinhole-allowed-from because the test-fw-a fixture declares `ingress from dmz` (the reverse-proxy path) and rules-manager validates every ingress against the target zone's pinhole-allowed-from. Dropping it makes test-fw-a un-installable — which is exactly what happened when these zones were first lifted out of the install template.

testAllowA._comment: Activated by network test.sh --deep. Bidirectional access with testAllowB validates inter-zone allow rules in both directions.
testAllowA.description: Deep-test zone A: bidirectional allow validation

testAllowB._comment: Activated by network test.sh --deep. Peer of testAllowA.
testAllowB.description: Deep-test zone B: bidirectional allow validation

testPinhole._comment: Activated by network test.sh --deep. testAllowA appears ONLY in pinhole-allowed-from, never in any access-to — that is what makes this the auto-pinhole path (#173): the consumer reaches it via a per-module rule, not zone-wide. Service-typed at tier 1 so the client->service reach is an UPWARD edge, exactly as the ADR-014 lattice intends.
